note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 by an independent auditor (authored none of the userns spec commits d8427e4380, b00e3c6710, 68b723ec4f, 7d11a51269). userns.Enter (internal/test/userns/userns_linux.go) re-executes the one test in a new user+net+mount namespace and returns false in the parent only after the child's own PASS line; a child failure, a zero-exit failure or a child that selected nothing fails the parent, and a child skip skips it, so the guard cannot turn a red into a green. Section 3.2.1.1: "When the IPv6 VPN traffic is to be transported to the BGP speaker using IPv6 tunneling (e.g., IPv6 MPLS LSPs, IPsec-protected IPv6 tunnels), the BGP speaker SHALL advertise a Next Hop Network Address field containing a VPN-IPv6 address - whose 8-octet RD is set to zero, and - whose 16-octet IPv6 address is set to the global IPv6 address of the advertising BGP speaker." TestRFC4659ConfiguredIPv6TransportNextHopWire changed by the guard only; the fixture's namespace refusal now fails instead of skipping, and rfc4659ConfiguredSettings gained `filter { export { final accept; } }` because the recipient is EBGP and RFC 8212 default-reject would otherwise keep the routes out of Adj-RIB-Out. That is an operator-path policy, not a relaxation: every assertion in rfc4659ReadConfiguredRoutes (exact zero RD, speaker-owned global for self, selected address for explicit, both grouping modes over TCP6 into a real Session) is unchanged. TestRFC4659LinkLocalPeeringPreservesUnspecifiedGlobalPair unchanged. {single-polarity: positive} stays correct: sender emission, not receiver rejection. Control-plane evidence only, not tunnel creation. Record (buildMPReachVPN revert) re-taken in 7d11a51269.
